notes_list.title: Alcohol Functional Group Tests
notes_list.basic_overview: Primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols can be distinguished using oxidation behavior and substitution-based tests, while phenols require separate tests.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Lucas reagent (conc HCl/ZnCl2) gives different rates of turbidity formation; chromic acid-type oxidation distinguishes primary/secondary alcohols from tertiary alcohols under common conditions.
notes_list.examples: Primary alcohol → aldehyde/acid depending oxidant; secondary → ketone; tertiary resists ordinary oxidation without C–C cleavage.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Lucas reagent is strongly acidic; temperature affects observed rate. Oxidation depends on reagent and water content.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Lucas test involves protonation, water departure and chloride capture; tertiary alcohols react faster because carbocation formation is easier.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Lucas test is qualitative kinetics: relative rate of turbidity formation reflects substitution mechanism under the test conditions.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not interpret Lucas test as an absolute structural proof without considering substrate and conditions.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
